e-3519.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
e-3519.problem:
Find the exact value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)$ without using a calculator.

*Hint: Use the fact that $\dfrac{\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}.$*
e-3519.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\sin(x-y) = \sin x\cos y - \cos x\sin y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $y = \dfrac{\pi}{4},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-3518.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
e-3518.problem: Express $\sin\left(x - 30^{\circ} \right )$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
e-3518.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u-v) = \sin u\cos v - \cos u\sin v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=30^{\circ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{30}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9983.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
e-9983.problem: Express $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
e-9983.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u+v) = \sin{u}\cos{v} + \cos{u}\sin{v}
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-{105}^{∘}={30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}.$*
after.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x={30}^{∘}$ and $y={135}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-{105}^{∘}={30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}.$*
content.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x={30}^{∘}$ and $y={135}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $\frac{5\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}.$*
after.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{6}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $\frac{5\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}.$*
content.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{6}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{12})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $\frac{11\pi }{12}=\frac{7\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{4}.$*
content.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x=\frac{7\pi }{6}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{4}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})?$
after.worked_solution:
The angle ${75}^{∘}$ is not a special angle. However, we can rewrite it as the sum of two special angles, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{75}^{∘}={45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We now recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x={45}^{∘}$ and $y={30}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}

Question 5
?

What is the exact value of sin⁡(75∘)?

a
6−24
b
3+24
c
6+24
d
6−32
e
2+14
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The angle 75∘ is not a special angle. However, we can rewrite it as the sum of two special angles, as follows:

75∘=45∘+30∘

We now recall the sum formula for sine:

sin⁡(x+y)=sin⁡xcos⁡y+cos⁡xsin⁡y

Applying the sum formula for sine with x=45∘ and y=30∘, we obtain

sin⁡(75∘)=sin⁡(45∘+30∘)=sin⁡45∘cos⁡30∘+cos⁡45∘sin⁡30∘=22⋅32+22⋅12=64+24=6+24.

content.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.problem: What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})?$
content.worked_solution:
The angle ${75}^{∘}$ is not a special angle. However, we can rewrite it as the sum of two special angles, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{75}^{∘}={45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We now recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x={45}^{∘}$ and $y={30}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={150}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{150}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

sin⁡(x−120∘)=

a
2(sin⁡x+cos⁡x)2
b
3sin⁡x−cos⁡x2
c
−2(sin⁡x+cos⁡x)2
d
−sin⁡x+3cos⁡x2
e
sin⁡x−3cos⁡x2

decision.explanation: sin(x−120°)=sin(x)cos(120°)−cos(x)sin(120°). Substituting cos(120°)=−1/2 and sin(120°)=√3/2 gives −(sin(x)+√3 cos(x))/2, option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={120}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{120}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{120}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall the difference formula for sine: sin⁡(u−v)=sin⁡ucos⁡v−cos⁡usin⁡v

Applying the difference formula for sine with u=x and v=120∘, we get sin⁡(x−120∘)=sin⁡xcos⁡120∘−cos⁡xsin⁡120∘=sin⁡x⋅(−12)−cos⁡x⋅(32)=−sin⁡x2−3cos⁡x2=−sin⁡x+3cos⁡x2.

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={120}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{120}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{120}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={135}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{135}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={45}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{45}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall the difference formula for sine:

sin⁡(u−v)=sin⁡ucos⁡v−cos⁡usin⁡v

Applying the difference formula for sine with u=x and v=45∘, we get

sin⁡(x−45∘)=sin⁡xcos⁡45∘−cos⁡xsin⁡45∘=sin⁡x⋅(22)−cos⁡x⋅(22)=2sin⁡x2−2cos⁡x2=22(sin⁡x−cos⁡x).

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms sin(x−45°)=(√2/2)sin(x)−(√2/2)cos(x)=(√2/2)(sin(x)−cos(x)), option b. Option c omits the factor √2 from the cosine term.

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={45}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{45}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 11
?

sin⁡(x+4π3)=

a
3cos⁡x+sin⁡x2
b
3sin⁡x−cos⁡x2
c
−sin⁡x+3cos⁡x2
d
sin⁡x+cos⁡x2
e
2sin⁡x+cos⁡x2
Submit

decision.explanation: sin(x+4π/3)=sin(x)cos(4π/3)+cos(x)sin(4π/3). Since cos(4π/3)=−1/2 and sin(4π/3)=−√3/2, this equals −(sin(x)+√3 cos(x))/2, option c.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{4\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\sqrt{3}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall the sum formula for sine: sin⁡(u+v)=sin⁡ucos⁡v+cos⁡usin⁡v

Applying the sum formula for sine with u=x and v=4π3, we get sin⁡(x+π6)=sin⁡xcos⁡(4π3)+cos⁡xsin⁡(4π3)=sin⁡x⋅(−12)+cos⁡x⋅(−32)=−sin⁡x2−3cos⁡x2=−sin⁡x+3cos⁡x2.

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{4\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\sqrt{3}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

sin⁡(x−π4)=

a
22(sin⁡x−cos⁡x)
b
22(sin⁡x+cos⁡x)
c
22(cos⁡x−sin⁡x)
d
32(sin⁡x−cos⁡x)
e
12(sin⁡x−cos⁡x)
Submit

decision.explanation: sin(x−π/4)=sin(x)cos(π/4)−cos(x)sin(π/4). Both special-angle values equal √2/2, giving (√2/2)(sin(x)−cos(x)), option a.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
content.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (0)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (1) \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{7\pi }{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}sin\,(x+\frac{7\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{7\pi }{4}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{7\pi }{4} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
